HeroName: Basileús Ioánnis IV Doúkas Láskaris, Emperor of Nicaea
Description: John IV is Theodore II’s son and inherited the Nicaean throne after his father’s death. His youth makes him dependent on regents and advisers without ensuring that those who claim to protect him lack ambitions of their own. Changes at court after Mouzalon’s murder make it harder to know which adults deserve trust. Michael’s influence grows while the Laskarid name still brings ceremonial respect. John cannot always understand what these rituals and disputes mean for his own life. He needs patient explanations rather than instructions merely to nod at an arrangement. Familiar relatives and attendants matter to him, and he wants his questions taken seriously. Safety means not being suddenly separated from those he knows and being able to trust tomorrow in promises made today.
Motivations: Receive trustworthy guidance about arrangements made in his name.
Keep contact with familiar people and have his questions answered.
Values: Protection must be dependable rather than merely a title.
Even a child should understand what others ask him to accept.
Fears: Being separated from familiar people without an explanation.
Those around him fighting one another over his imperial position.
SpeechStyle: Young and cautious; checks promises repeatedly and looks to familiar people for reassurance.
